items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the interviewer ('[INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe') and the subject as Jon-Erik Kellso. No personal relationship beyond the interview context is described.

ctx.x: Jon was interviewed on September 12, 1997 in Chautauqua, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe. We’re filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m pleased to have Jon-Erik Kellso, trumpeter and jazz musician with us today. So let’s be honest, what’s a nice young man like you doing playing jazz music?

Oh, well, I got interested when I was really young. My parents were both into the Swing Era music, you know they grew up during that time and they had a lot of good old records around the house, so when I was about ten years old I got interested in playing the trumpet, and then after I decided to play trumpet I found out that my father was a trumpet player and had played in some swing bands during the World War II days. And I found some of his old records around, and got interested in it.
